note: Baseline: same time yesterday (lag 144). ACF at lag 144 is 0.88, so this is the bar every model must beat.
ARIMA starting point: PACF cuts off after lag 2, so ARMA(2,1) errors; 8 daily and 4 weekly Fourier pairs as a moderate first guess at seasonal shape.
LSTM starting point: one-day window (ACF 0.88 at lag 144), single layer of 64 units as a small model for ~5.3k training windows; Adam 1e-3 with early stopping.
TCN starting point: same one-day window as the LSTM for a fair first comparison; 6 levels of kernel 3 give a 253-step receptive field covering the window; 32 channels, dropout 0.1.
Round 1: daily harmonics 8 -> 16. The daily profile is sharp (17x peak-to-trough in raw traffic), so 8 Fourier pairs may be too smooth to follow the morning ramp and evening drop.

Round 1: lookback 144 -> 1008. ACF is 0.84 at one week vs 0.74 at three days, so a week of context should let the LSTM separate weekday and weekend behaviour; the first run was still improving at epoch 21, so capacity to use more context is plausible.

Round 1: channels 32 -> 16. The first TCN took 31 s/epoch on 2 CPU cores (6x the LSTM) and peaked at epoch 8; test whether accuracy holds with about a quarter of the convolution cost, which would make week-long receptive fields affordable.

Round 2: weekly harmonics 4 -> 8 (keeping 16 daily). Weekly seasonal strength was 0.63 in the EDA, and 4 pairs may be too coarse to shape the weekday/weekend contrast; round 1 showed extra Fourier detail is supported by AIC.

Round 2: back to lookback 144 (1008 cost 28x the time for 3% MAE and worse MAPE). Learning rate 1e-3 -> 5e-4 with patience 10 and up to 80 epochs: the first LSTM was still improving but its validation loss was noisy, so early stopping likely ended it on noise.
Round 2: max epochs 40 -> 80. The 16-channel TCN beat the 32-channel one and was still improving when it hit the 40-epoch cap (best epoch 34).

Round 2b: repeat of round 2 after fixing the regressors. Round 2 failed with zero optimiser iterations because weekly harmonic 7 equals daily harmonic 1 (1008 = 7 x 144), making the Fourier columns collinear; duplicated weekly harmonics are now dropped (14 weekly columns instead of 16).

Round 3: d 0 -> 1 on the round-1 configuration. The converged d=0 fit has an AR root of modulus 1.04 with MA -0.62, i.e. near-unit-root errors: after removing the cycles the level drifts, consistent with the holiday and December trend shifts in the EDA. Differencing tests whether modelling that drift directly helps.

Round 4 (final ARIMA): combine the two best changes, d=1 (round 3: best RMSE) and 8 weekly harmonics with duplicates removed (round 2b: best MAE). All converged ARIMA variants are within 1.5% MAE, so ARIMA tuning stops after this under the <1% improvement rule.

Round 3: one layer -> two stacked layers with dropout 0.1. The LSTM trails ARIMA and TCN by ~9% and its training loss plateaued near 0.020 like the TCN's, so test whether hierarchical depth helps rather than more training time.

Round 3: lookback 144 -> 1008 with 8 levels (receptive field 1021). Tests Bai et al.'s claim that TCNs use long memory effectively, and the EDA's 0.84 ACF at one week; the LSTM could not exploit a week of context efficiently, and 16 channels make this affordable.
